ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Causal feature warping from one RGB frame and an event voxel stream
PROPOSAL: Encode I_t with a frozen SegFormer-B2 and the events since t-Δt with a small ResNet-18 voxel encoder. A decoder receives a sinusoidal embedding of the offset δt, predicts the displacement of RGB features toward the target time, and emits the semantic map. Train on DSEC-Semantic with offsets sampled uniformly in (0, Δt], check transfer on DDD17 and MVSEC, and report mIoU in 5 offset bins with 3 seeds, plus a breakdown on person, rider and car pixels.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward of the segmentation at t; an event-only segmenter of equal size; RGB-event fusion that targets the frame at t only; a non-causal interpolation model given the future frame, as an upper reference.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Gains over copy-forward should grow with δt and concentrate on moving classes, reaching roughly 4 mIoU points at the longest offset. It could fail if event noise at night makes the displacement head collapse toward the identity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct RGB-event fusion with a SegFormer-B5 backbone and a sweep over input settings
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune SegFormer-B5 end to end with a ResNet-50 voxel encoder, concatenating the two feature streams with an embedding of the offset δt before a convolutional decoder. Train on DSEC-Semantic with offsets sampled uniformly in (0, Δt], repeating the run for 6 voxel bin counts and 3 learning rates, and report mIoU in 5 offset bins with 5 seeds, plus a breakdown on person, rider and car pixels of the validation split.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward of the segmentation at t; an event-only segmenter on the same backbone; fusion that targets the frame at t only; a version with the offset embedding removed, as a reference.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The sweep should show a best bin count near 10 and a spread of about 2 mIoU over learning rates, with gains over copy-forward at long offsets. It may fail if the validation split holds too few moving pedestrians to rank the settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous-time latent rollout for semantic maps in the blind interval
PROPOSAL: Represent the scene at t as a latent from a Swin-T encoder on I_t, then advance it with a neural ordinary differential equation driven by features from a sparse-convolution event encoder, so the state can be decoded at any δt. Train on DSEC-Semantic with 3 seeds and a loss that emphasizes long offsets, and test transfer to DDD17, and measure mIoU against offset as well as temporal consistency of consecutive predictions.
CONTROLS: A discrete-step recurrent rollout with fixed offsets; an optical-flow warp of the prediction at t using event-derived flow; removal of the event input to isolate its contribution; the non-causal bidirectional reference.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The continuous rollout should match the recurrent baseline at trained offsets and beat it at unseen offsets by about 2 mIoU. It could fail if the solver drifts over long intervals, giving blurred object boundaries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensor-transfer test of event-driven latent rollout with a recurrent state update
PROPOSAL: Represent the scene at t as a latent from a Swin-T encoder on I_t, then advance it with a gated recurrent update driven by features from a sparse-convolution event encoder, decoding the state at 8 offset values. Train on DSEC-Semantic, DDD17 and MVSEC in turn with 3 seeds and a second loss weighting, and measure mIoU against offset, temporal consistency of consecutive predictions, and transfer from each sensor to the others.
CONTROLS: A single-step prediction that skips the recurrent update; an optical-flow warp of the prediction at t using event-derived flow; the event-free variant of the recurrent model; the non-causal bidirectional reference.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Training on the sensor with the highest event rate should transfer best, losing about 3 mIoU on the other two sensors. It might fail if label sets differ enough between the corpora that transfer scores mostly reflect taxonomy mismatch.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-supervised event pretraining from converted driving video before segmentation
PROPOSAL: Convert Cityscapes-sequence and KITTI-360 clips into synthetic event streams with an event simulator, pretrain an event encoder to forecast the next RGB-feature map from I_t and the events, then fine-tune on DSEC-Semantic with a time embedding for δt. Use a ViT-S backbone with 3 seeds, compare 3 pretraining lengths, and report mIoU at 5 offsets together with an analysis of failures on newly appearing objects.
CONTROLS: Training from scratch on DSEC-Semantic alone; pretraining on RGB frames only with no events; an event-only segmenter; copy-forward of the segmentation at t.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Pretraining should help most where labeled event data is scarce, adding about 3 mIoU on appearing objects. It may fail if the simulator's noise statistics differ from real sensors and the benefit vanishes after fine-tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-student event pretraining from converted Cityscapes-sequence video
PROPOSAL: Convert Cityscapes-sequence clips into synthetic event streams with an event simulator, pretrain a ViT-L teacher to forecast the next RGB-feature map from I_t and the events, distill it into a ViT-S student, then fine-tune the student on DSEC-Semantic with a time embedding for δt. Run 3 seeds for the teacher and 3 for the student, compare 5 pretraining lengths, using 2 distillation temperatures, and report mIoU at 5 offsets with an analysis of failures on newly appearing objects.
CONTROLS: Training from scratch on DSEC-Semantic alone; a ViT-S student pretrained directly without the teacher; an event-only segmenter; copy-forward of the segmentation at t.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The distilled student should gain about 3 mIoU on appearing objects over scratch training. It may fail if teacher gains do not transfer through distillation, leaving the student near the scratch baseline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight offset-conditioned head on frozen segmentation features
PROPOSAL: Keep a pretrained SegFormer-B0 frozen on I_t and train only a small head that fuses its features with a 2-channel event count image and a scalar embedding of δt. Use DSEC-Semantic, sample offsets uniformly, and compare a linear head, a 3-layer convolutional head and a gated head. Report mIoU in 4 offset bins with 5 seeds, and examine whether the head relies on events by shuffling them across clips.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward of the segmentation at t; the same head fed with a zero event image; a head given the offset only; an event-only model of matched parameter count. Each is trained with the same schedule.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The convolutional head should recover most of the gap between copy-forward and a fully fine-tuned model, to within 2 mIoU. It could fail if frozen features lack the spatial detail needed to place moving boundaries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-conditioned fusion on partly tuned features with attention and convolutional heads
PROPOSAL: Unfreeze the last 2 stages of a pretrained SegFormer-B2 on I_t and train heads that fuse its features with a 2-channel event count image and a scalar embedding of δt. Use DSEC-Semantic with DDD17 held out, sample offsets uniformly, and compare a convolutional head, an attention head and 2 hybrids. Report mIoU in 4 offset bins with 3 seeds, and examine whether the heads rely on events by shuffling them across clips.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward of the segmentation at t; the same heads fed with a zero event image; a head given the offset only; a fully frozen backbone with the convolutional head, for comparison.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Attention heads should win at long offsets by about 1 mIoU, though most designs will land within the noise between seeds. It could fail if DDD17 labels are too coarse to separate the designs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing event representations for blind-interval segmentation
PROPOSAL: Compare voxel grids, time surfaces and spike tensors as inputs to the same fusion network built on a ConvNeXt-T RGB encoder with an offset embedding. Train on DSEC-Semantic and MVSEC with the target label at δt drawn from the 20 Hz label timestamps, and tune the number of temporal bins in 3 settings per representation. Report mIoU at 5 offsets with 3 seeds and the relation between event rate and accuracy per region.
CONTROLS: A copy-forward predictor at t; a model that uses the RGB frame only; a representation with polarity removed; the non-causal interpolation reference using the following frame.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Voxel grids should lead at short offsets while time surfaces help at long ones, with a spread near 2 mIoU. It might fail if the differences vanish once the number of bins is tuned for each representation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Survey of event representations with a ConvNeXt-B encoder on DSEC-Semantic
PROPOSAL: Compare 6 representations, including voxel grids, time surfaces, spike tensors, event frames, learned embeddings and polarity-split stacks, as inputs to a fusion network built on a ConvNeXt-B RGB encoder with an offset embedding. Train on DSEC-Semantic with the target label at δt drawn from the 20 Hz label timestamps, tune the number of temporal bins in 5 settings per representation, and report mIoU at 5 offsets with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: A copy-forward predictor at t; a model that uses the RGB frame only; a representation with polarity removed; a ConvNeXt-T version of the best representation, to check size sensitivity.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Rankings among representations should be stable over seeds, with a spread near 2 mIoU between best and worst. It might fail if bin tuning narrows the spread below the seed-to-seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Query-based decoder with time-conditioned queries for appearing objects
PROPOSAL: Build a Mask2Former-style decoder on a Swin-T encoder of I_t whose object queries are modulated by an embedding of δt and cross-attend to event tokens from a sparse transformer. Train on DSEC-Semantic, with a DDD17 split held out, using a loss up-weighting classes that are absent at t but present at the target time, with 3 seeds, and report mIoU on appearing instances against offset along with false-positive rates on static regions.
CONTROLS: A per-pixel decoder with the same encoders; queries without time modulation; a model that never sees events; the copy-forward segmentation at t. All use one training schedule.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The time-modulated queries should add 3 to 5 mIoU on newly appearing instances at the longest offsets. It could fail if the number of appearing objects is too small for stable estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Query-based event decoders on Swin-L encoders with staged pretraining on sensor data
PROPOSAL: Build a Mask2Former-style decoder on a Swin-L encoder of I_t whose object queries are modulated by an embedding of δt and cross-attend to event tokens from a sparse transformer. Pretrain on MVSEC and DDD17, then fine-tune on DSEC-Semantic with a loss up-weighting appearing classes, using 3 seeds and 2 pretraining lengths, and report mIoU on appearing instances against offset along with false-positive rates on static regions.
CONTROLS: A per-pixel decoder with the same encoders; queries without time modulation; a model that never sees events; fine-tuning without the pretraining stage. All use one schedule and one data order.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Time modulation should add 3 to 5 mIoU on appearing instances, with pretraining adding a little more. It could fail if label conventions differ so much between corpora that pretraining blurs the appearing classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation protocol for blind-interval accuracy using stretched frame gaps
PROPOSAL: Because labels exist only at 20 Hz, stretch the gap by feeding I_t and events spanning 2, 3 and 5 label intervals, then score the predictions against the intermediate labels. Train one ResNet-34 fusion network with an offset embedding on DSEC-Semantic and DDD17, with 3 seeds, and report mIoU against true elapsed time, along with a check that accuracy at stretched offsets matches accuracy at native ones.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward at t; the fusion network without events; a network trained only on native 20 Hz gaps and tested on stretched ones; the non-causal interpolation reference.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Accuracy should decay smoothly with elapsed time, roughly 1.5 mIoU per label interval. It could fail if stretching creates motion statistics that differ from real long gaps, so the protocol is not trustworthy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gap-specific models for blind-interval accuracy on stretched frame gaps
PROPOSAL: Because labels exist only at 20 Hz, stretch the gap by feeding I_t and events spanning 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 label intervals, and train a separate ResNet-34 fusion network for each gap on DSEC-Semantic with no offset embedding. Score each against the intermediate labels with 5 seeds and report mIoU against true elapsed time, along with a check that specialized models beat a shared one at their own gap.
CONTROLS: Copy-forward at t; the same networks without events; one shared network with an offset embedding trained over all gaps; the non-causal interpolation reference.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Specialized models should lead the shared one by about 1 mIoU at their own gap and fall behind it elsewhere. It could fail if per-gap training sets are too small, leaving the specialists under-trained.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Privileged-teacher distillation from a non-causal model into a causal student
PROPOSAL: Train a Swin-B teacher that sees I_t, the events and the future frame I_{t+Δt}, then distill its soft maps at randomly drawn offsets into a causal student with a Swin-T encoder that sees only I_t and events. Use DSEC-Semantic with 10 percent of the clips held out, a temperature of 2 in the distillation loss, and 3 seeds, and report mIoU in 5 offset bins together with the fraction of the teacher-student gap that is closed.
CONTROLS: A student trained on hard labels only; a student distilled from an RGB-only teacher; the teacher itself as an upper reference; copy-forward of the segmentation at t.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The student should close roughly half of the gap between the label-trained student and the teacher, mainly at long offsets. It could fail if the teacher's reliance on the future frame makes its targets impossible to imitate causally.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-round self-distillation of causal students on three event corpora
PROPOSAL: Train a causal Swin-T student on I_t and events with hard labels, then use it as the teacher for the next round of an identical student, repeating for 3 rounds with soft maps at randomly drawn offsets and a temperature of 2. Use DSEC-Semantic, DDD17 and MVSEC with 3 seeds, and report mIoU against offset together with the gain per round and the agreement between consecutive students.
CONTROLS: A student trained on hard labels only; a student distilled from an RGB-only teacher; a larger non-causal teacher as an upper reference; copy-forward of the segmentation at t.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Gains should be positive in round 1 at about 2 mIoU, then flatten by round 3. It could fail if students inherit each other's errors on appearing objects and the agreement rises without any accuracy gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event noise and night robustness through learned denoising and augmentation
PROPOSAL: Add a small denoising front end to the event encoder trained with contrast-based augmentation: randomly dropping events, injecting uniform background activity, and jittering timestamps. Train a ResNet-34 fusion model on DSEC-Semantic day sequences with 10 percent held out for validation, test on night sequences and on MVSEC with 3 seeds, and report mIoU in 5 offset bins in clean and corrupted settings, with attention maps showing which events drive the prediction.
CONTROLS: The same model without denoising; augmentation without the front end; a model trained directly on night sequences; copy-forward at t.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Denoising with augmentation should hold mIoU at night within 3 points of day performance, where the plain model drops by about 8. It could fail if learned filtering discards the sparse events from small, fast pedestrians.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Corruption-matched training of event fusion models on DSEC-Semantic
PROPOSAL: Retrain a ResNet-34 fusion model on DSEC-Semantic day sequences under 5 corruption types: random event dropping, uniform background activity, timestamp jitter, polarity flips and hot pixels, each at 5 severity levels. Test on night sequences with 3 seeds, and report mIoU against offset for models trained and tested at matched or mismatched severity, with a Swin-B encoder repeated for the 2 most damaging types.
CONTROLS: A model trained on clean data only; a model trained on all corruptions mixed; a model trained directly on night sequences; copy-forward at t.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Matched-severity training should recover about 5 of the 8 points lost at night by the clean model. It could fail if the synthetic corruptions do not resemble night noise, so recovery on night sequences is small.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibrating prediction confidence as a function of the offset
PROPOSAL: Fit a temperature and a per-class bias on top of a trained fusion network for each δt bin, using a held-out split of DSEC-Semantic, and measure expected calibration error and risk-coverage curves against elapsed time. Use a ResNet-34 encoder with an offset embedding, 3 seeds, and report whether low-confidence regions coincide with newly appearing or occluded objects.
CONTROLS: An uncalibrated network; a single global temperature; a network with a learned confidence head trained jointly; copy-forward of the segmentation at t with a constant confidence.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Calibration error should fall by about a third with offset-specific temperatures and concentrate on appearing objects. It could fail if the held-out split is too small to fit stable biases at long offsets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty estimation by ensembles and dropout over offsets on DSEC-Semantic and MVSEC
PROPOSAL: Train ensembles of 5 fusion networks with different seeds and compare them to Monte Carlo dropout with 10 passes, on DSEC-Semantic and MVSEC, measuring expected calibration error and risk-coverage curves against elapsed time. Use a ResNet-34 encoder with an offset embedding, and report whether low-confidence regions coincide with newly appearing or occluded objects.
CONTROLS: A single uncalibrated network; one global temperature; a network with a learned confidence head trained jointly; copy-forward of the segmentation at t with a constant confidence.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Ensembles should cut calibration error by about a third relative to a single network, concentrated on appearing objects. It could fail if members agree too closely to expose the information that is missing.
